{"type":"text","timestamp":1794668797431,"sessionID":"ses_e25695e53ffeCP1FWea7oRbliE","part":{"id":"prt_1da989dc8001d8aC0Zw47xkpud","messageID":"msg_1da9881f4001rBpaFPtQHmmJyo","sessionID":"ses_e25695e53ffeCP1FWea7oRbliE","type":"text","text":"The episode is over. The rover finished alive with about 10% battery, and the position readings put it at base.\n\n**Sampled, all before their deadlines:** t5 (2), t1 (1), t3 (2), t2 (1) and d1 (2), for 8 points. d1 was the target discovered partway through the mission.\n\n**Missed:** t4 (1 point). The sample at tick 24 failed because the rover wasn't close enough. In telemetry, wheel slip on bedrock jumped to about 18% on the drive just before it, so the ground change had probably happened. That drive came up roughly 0.6 m short of t4. I didn't go back for t4's late value of 0.25: the extra driving and the sample would have taken too much of the remaining battery, and running it to zero scores nothing.\n\n**Return to base:** the drive back was based on positions I estimated without fixes, and it seemed to stop about 0.8 m from base, just outside the 0.75 m radius. I averaged about a dozen noisy position fixes to confirm that, then sent a 1 m correction. Afterwards the fixes averaged about (19.95, 20.0), with base at (20, 20). The score uses the true position, which telemetry can't show exactly.\n\n**Expected score:** 8 of 9 possible points, about 0.89. That counts the full 1.0 for ending at base. No second discovery ever appeared.","time":{"start":1794668797384,"end":1794668797426}}}
